title: Maximum Average Pass Ratio
summary: Given a school with classes having varying numbers of students and pass rates, and an additional number of guaranteed-pass students, determine the best assignment of these students to classes to maximize the overall pass rate.
statement: Given a school with classes having varying numbers of students and pass rates, and an additional number of guaranteed-pass students, determine the best assignment of these students to classes to maximize the overall pass rate. The pass rate of a class is the number of students who pass divided by the total number of students. The goal is to find the highest possible average pass rate after assigning the extra students.
constraints: Each class is [passed,total] with at least one passing student.
Assign every guaranteed-pass extra student to maximize the final average; answers use floating tolerance.
hints: Measure how much one extra passing student improves each class ratio.
Always give the next student to the class with the largest current marginal gain.
Store negative gains in a min-heap and recompute a class gain after assignment.
Marginal gains diminish for each class, so the exchange argument makes the largest available gain optimal at every step.
editorial: Marginal gains diminish for each class, so the exchange argument makes the largest available gain optimal at every step.

tests.explanation: Both students go to the first class, producing average (3/4+3/5+1)/3.
Repeatedly choosing the largest marginal ratio increase gives approximately 0.53485.
